title: Quick follow-up: decision levers, procurement path, and SLA targets
text:
Quick follow-up: decision levers, procurement path, and SLA targets

["From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Yates <sam.yates@prioryhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 15:09:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up: decision levers, procurement path, and SLA targets

Hi Sam —

Great to meet today — thanks for the time. Short follow-up with the concrete items we discussed so we’re aligned on decision levers and next steps. I put the asks below so you can loop in procurement/legal and the econ buyer.

Summary from our call:
- Primary use case: near-real-time summarization and triage of clinician notes for 2 pilot clinics (~500k tokens/day peak).
- Key levers you called out: latency (user-facing p95), per-inference cost, data residency/segmentation, and compliance evidence (audit logs/SOC reports).

Questions / confirmation needed (can you confirm or forward to the right person?):
1) Economic buyer: who will sign the PO? You mentioned Laura Kim (Finance) might own budget — can you confirm and share her preferred procurement contact?
2) Latency target: from your product team, does <120ms p95 for inference meet the product requirement, or do we need to aim for <100ms p95? Any absolute tail limits we should know about?
3) Cost envelope: what is the target unit economics for inference you'd consider acceptable for pilot vs. production (e.g., target cost per 1M tokens or total monthly budget)?
4) Deployment preference: hosted (Redwood API) vs Dedicated vs Private VPC — you indicated security leaning toward private/VPC for PHI; is Private required for procurement or adequate as a canary (Dedicated with encryption in transit + strict contract)?
5) SLA baseline: is 99.9% available acceptable for pilot, or are you looking for 99.95+/commercial SLAs from day one? Any minimum incident response times or audit needs?

Next steps from our side:
- I can share our SOC2 report and a short pilot SOW (attached).
- If you confirm econ buyer + procurement contact, we’ll prepare a pilot quote and a 30-day scoped performance runbook showing expected p95 latency and cost profile for the pilot clinics.
- Technical deep-dive: proposing Wed 26 May or Thu 27 May — 60 minutes to validate perf tests and data flow.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_Report_2026.pdf (pdf), Pilot_SOW_template.docx (docx)

Thanks — I’ll wait for the procurement/legal contacts and any updates on the latency/cost targets so we can size the pilot appropriately.

Best,
Rishi
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0118

", 'From: Sam Yates <sam.yates@prioryhealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Kim <laura.kim@prioryhealth.com>, Rajiv Gupta <rajiv.gupta@prioryhealth.com>, procurement@prioryhealth.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: decision levers, procurement path, and SLA targets

Rishi —

Thanks for the crisp recap and for sending the SOC2 and SOW. Quick answers below and I copied the people who should be in the loop.

1) Economic buyer: Confirmed — Laura Kim (cc’d) is the economic buyer and will own the PO. Laura, Rajiv (legal) and the procurement alias are the primary procurement path.
2) Latency: Product target is 120ms p95 for the first pilot. If you can reliably deliver <120ms p95, we’re comfortable; long-term we’d like to see <100ms but that’s a Phase 2 target. Also call out cold-start behavior — anything >250ms in the 99th percentile is a showstopper.
3) Cost: We’re very cost-sensitive. Pilot budget is capped at $8k/month for the service (not including integration engineering). For production we’ll revisit based on value. Please propose a pilot pricing option that keeps us under that cap.
4) Deployment: Security prefers Private VPC for PHI. For procurement purposes, Private VPC or a dedicated customer VPC in a cloud region where we control network egress is basically required — hosted API won’t pass our compliance bar for the pilot.
5) SLA: For pilot we can accept 99.9% but legal will ask for a path to commercial SLAs (>=99.95) for production. Audit logs and retention policy details are required up front.

Procurement timeline: procurement@ has an intake form attached (link below). We’re targeting a 6–8 week procurement window for the pilot (vendor review, security questionnaire, PO).

Link to intake/questionnaire: https://docs.prioryhealth.com/procurement/questionnaire-2027

Laura — looping you in for approval and to confirm the procurement lead we should work with. Rajiv — if you want any specific contract language redlines up front, let us know; otherwise we’ll provide a standard pilot MSA and SOW.

Thanks — happy to jump on a follow-up with procurement or legal.

Best,
Sam
VP Product — Priory Health
sam.yates@prioryhealth.com

', 'From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Yates <sam.yates@prioryhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Kim <laura.kim@prioryhealth.com>, Rajiv Gupta <rajiv.gupta@prioryhealth.com>, procurement@prioryhealth.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 13:58:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: decision levers, procurement path, and SLA targets

Sam / Laura / Rajiv —

Appreciate the clarified targets — this is very actionable. Quick notes on how Redwood would approach the pilot to meet your constraints:

- Latency: We can commit to a benchmarking plan that demonstrates <120ms p95 in your target region using Dedicated capacity sized to your expected concurrency. We’ll include cold-start mitigation (warmup pools) to keep 99th percentile below 250ms for the pilot.
- Cost: We’ll design a 30-day pilot quote that targets staying under $8k/mo by optimizing batching, KV caching, and an autoscale profile tuned to clinic hours. The quote will include a line for burst capacity and a modeled cost appendix.
- Deployment: Private VPC is supported — we’ll provide a deployment runbook that covers network peering, KMS integration, and ingest controls. For the procurement questionnaire, attached are the SOC2 report and a pilot SOW template.
- SLA: Pilot contract will include 99.9% availability and an agreed remediation plan; we’ll add a migration path and pricing delta to move to 99.95+ for production.

Next actions I’ll take this week:
1) Marissa — can you prepare a draft pilot quote + runbook referencing the $8k cap and propose a 30-day scope?
2) Soojin — please pull our private VPC checklist and any region-specific notes for the west coast region.
3) Sam/Laura/procurement — if you can send any additional intake files or the preferred PO template, we’ll slot them in.

Proposed technical deep-dive: Wed 26 May, 11:00am PT — 60 mins (perf test plan + network sketch). If that works I’ll send a calendar invite with an agenda.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this to pilot.

Best,
Rishi

Subject: Fwd: Quick follow-up: decision levers, procurement path, and SLA targets

Marissa / Soojin — forwarding the thread from Priory (Sam/Laura/Rajiv). Key constraints to incorporate into the pilot quote and runbook:
- p95 target: <120ms for pilot; long-term <100ms.
- 99th percentile hard cap: <250ms.
- Budget cap for pilot: $8k/month.
- Deployment: Private VPC required for PHI + KMS integration + audit logs retention.
- Procurement timeline: 6–8 weeks; intake form at the link in Sam's email.

Marissa — please draft a pilot quote that includes: Dedicated/private VPC option, modeled cost appendix hitting <$8k/mo, and a line item for a 30-day performance pilot. If you can include an optional add-on for a 99.95 SLA (price delta) that would be great.

Soojin — please attach the private VPC checklist and region notes. I’ve attached the SOC2 and SOW again.

Attachments (forwarded): Redwood_SOC2_Report_2026.pdf, Pilot_SOW_template.docx

Thanks — can you both have a draft ready by EOD Wed so I can send to procurement?

Rishi
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
